question.stem: A sealed container at rest holds helium gas. Each helium atom has a mass of $6.64 \times 10^{-27}$ kg. The atoms move randomly, with a root-mean-square (rms) speed of 1.37 $\text{km s}^{-1}$. Helium behaves as an ideal monatomic gas.

parts.label: a
parts.question: State the average velocity of the helium atoms.
markscheme: zero: the atoms move equally in all directions, so their velocities (vectors) cancel ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Explain why the rms speed, rather than the average velocity, is used in the equation for the pressure of an ideal gas.
markscheme: the average velocity is zero, so it cannot describe how hard or how often the atoms hit the walls ✓
the momentum change in each collision and the rate of collisions both depend on the speed, so the pressure depends on the mean of the squares of the speeds, whose square root is the rms speed ✓

parts.label: c
parts.question: Determine the temperature of the helium.

mistakes.feedback: The average kinetic energy of an atom of an ideal monatomic gas is (3/2)kBT, not kBT.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The density of the helium is 0.16 $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. Calculate the pressure of the helium.

mistakes.feedback: P = (1/3)ρv²rms: remember the factor of one third.

vr.what: rms speed of the helium atoms

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: The 2028 guidance contrasts rms velocity with average VELOCITY. A speed (e.g. "about 1.3 km/s") earns no mark.

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: Pressure ∝ (momentum change per collision) × (collision rate), both ∝ v, so ∝ the mean of v², which is not zero.

parts.label: c
parts.examinerNote: The average kinetic energy uses the mean square speed, so the rms speed goes into ½mv². The rms speed must be in m s⁻¹.

parts.label: d
parts.examinerNote: The data-booklet equation; about atmospheric pressure.
